item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Not verified: Hop On Has Missed Both Deadlines
item.description: Hop On Management has missed two court-upheld deadlines to convene Wang Fuk Court homeowners while 1,984 displaced households face a June 30 buyback cutoff they cannot collectively scrutinize.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Not verified: HK$17 Gate, Queue Before Eight
item.description: The Observatory's extreme heat warning means the public pool queue and the nearest air-conditioned mall are where this Saturday's outdoor plans actually end up.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Not verified: 71.5 Per Cent, One Market Short
item.description: May's home-sales-value surge is a wealth-tier event; the secondary market where most HK families buy has not moved with it, and Beijing's capital controls are the reason.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Not verified: HK$4.6 Billion Keeps the Counter Open
item.description: Home prices logged an eleventh consecutive monthly gain; the public post office serving the same streets needs HK$4.6 billion from the government to avoid service cuts through next year.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Not verified: CLP's June Bill Lands on 18,000 Permit Holders
item.description: The government's proposed 10,000 ride-hailing permits and CLP's 5.4% June fuel increase land on the same operators, who are still paying for the market they expected to keep.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Not verified: Goldman's 15 Percent, Friday's Gazette
item.description: Goldman's fifteen percent revision hits estate agent windows on the same Friday the civil service investigation regulation lands, handing two very different papers to two very different readers.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Not verified: Four Certified. 110,000 Still Waiting.
item.description: Four units certified from a backlog of 110,000 illegal flats, as secondary prices are forecast to rise 11% this year: the owners holding unregistered paper are watching a recovery they cannot access.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Not verified: The Rate the Recovery Skipped
item.description: Hong Kong's 5.9% Q1 growth is real, IMF-endorsed, and politically settled; it has not reached the credit windows and minimum-order thresholds where small operators run their calculations.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Not verified: The Gap the Stall Pays
item.description: Hong Kong printed 5.9 percent GDP growth for Q1 and raised its inflation forecast in the same week; both numbers are accurate, and they reach different addresses.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Not verified: The Q1 Number That Lands Unevenly
item.description: Hong Kong's 5.9% Q1 growth and the government's inflation forecast revision arrived in the same week; they do not describe the same households.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Not verified: When the Cut Arrives One Generation Late
item.description: The operators who gain from the May toll cut are the same families financing university for children entering a job market down sixty percent.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Not verified: What S&P's Eight Percent Does Not Say
item.description: S&P forecasts 8-10% home price growth while New World moves to sell $2 billion in assets, leaving mass-market buyers with two stories that do not add up.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung
